notes: The Wadsworth CLEP listings are public and reachable, but they carry no useful data for this thesis. The printable node I opened (https://www.wadsworth.org/node/564584/printable/print) shows one record: Project ID 104915, OmniSeq Inc, analyte 'OmniSeq INSIGHT (modification)', method NGS and IHC, FFPE tissue, oncology, status Approved, NY facility ID 9025. The record names no instrument and carries no approval date. The base URL https://www.wadsworth.org/regulatory/clep/approved-ldts returned a 404. WebSearch with site:wadsworth.org returned no Natera, Signatera, Guardant, Caris, Tempus, GeneDx or Foundation entries and no NovaSeq mentions. It returned only the risk attestation forms and facility list pages. I ran 4 tool calls and did not run the remaining per-company searches. Those searches would probably repeat this result, because the index does not seem to cover the node pages. The 'modification' label does not distinguish a sequencer change from any other change. The Risk Attestation Form does list instrumentation as one possible type of modification, but the public listing does not show which kind occurred. Without instrument names or dates, I cannot date any lab's move to the NovaSeq X from this source.
how_to_mine: Not recommended. If someone tries anyway, they would need to crawl the paginated list at https://www.wadsworth.org/regulatory/clep/approved-labs?page=N and the node/NNNNNN/printable/print pages. They would then filter facility names (Natera, Guardant, Caris, Tempus, GeneDx, Foundation Medicine) and keep only entries whose analyte ends in '(modification)'. The listing has no dates and no instruments. Even a complete crawl would give only a count of modifications, not the instrument change. A real answer would need a FOIA or CLEP request for the applications, and the lab validation packets are not public.
